questions.question: Gross margin dropped sharply last quarter. What caused it?
questions.answer: Gross margin dropped from 30.54% in 2026-Q2 to 24.51% in 2026-Q3. Main cause: Calder Metals’ product costs rose much faster than selling prices, crushing Metals profit. Metals decomposition shows $6.34M adverse price effect; volume and mix partly offset it. Product-level evidence shows same pattern across top losses: Metals item 8 cost/unit rose $553.67 to $653.33 while net price rose only $776.43

questions.question: Operating margin was much lower in Q3 2026 than in Q2 2026. Find the main driver.
questions.answer: Main driver: higher cost of Metals products, concentrated in West. Operating margin dropped from 11.59% to 4.67% (6.92 percentage points). Revenue increased, but gross profit fell $5.52M; expenses also rose, but were not primary. Metals COGS increased while category revenue grew, and unit cost rose about 18% across all listed Calder Metals items. Based on completed-order and expense totals for Q2

questions.question: Why was the average discount rate higher in Q2 2026 than in Q1 2026?
questions.answer: Discount rate increased from 7.25% in Q1 2026 to 7.53% in Q2, up 0.28 percentage points. Discounts grew 17.7%, outpacing pre-discount sales growth of 13.3%. SMB discounting intensified most: discount dollars rose 198.9% while pre-discount sales increased from $3.40M to $3.67M. Enterprise drove more of the absolute discount-dollar increase: +$871,593 versus SMB +$270,180.

questions.question: Discounts given jumped in the second quarter of 2026. Which customers drove that?
questions.answer: Comparison uses Q2 versus Q1; dollars, completed orders. Changes reflect both sales volume and discounting; not discount rate alone.

questions.question: Are customers paying later than they used to in 2026? If so, where is the problem?
questions.answer: Yes. Payments on 2026-issued invoices were later, driven by North: average payment shifted from 2.03 days before due in 2025 to 1.52 days after due in 2026. East, South, and West still paid about 2 days early. Comparison uses invoices issued in each year; 2026 covers data through September 30. Customer-level evidence did not identify the specific North customers causing the shift.

questions.question: Collections seem to have slowed since April 2026. Which region is responsible?
questions.answer: No single region clearly responsible for slower collections after April. Monthly collected dollars fluctuate by region; DSO and days-late averages do not show consistent broad deterioration. Collected dollars alone can reflect invoice volume, not collection speed. Evidence covers paid invoices by payment month; unpaid overdue invoices are excluded.
